questions.text: Why can an ELF executable still run after its section header table has been removed?

options.A: The loader uses program headers to map segments into memory.
options.B: The loader reconstructs section headers from every instruction.
options.C: The symbol table provides all memory mappings needed to load it.
options.D: The loader treats the entire file as one executable code section.

questions.explanation: Program headers describe the loader’s segment mappings. Section headers support the linking and analysis view and can be absent from an executable.

questions.text: A function symbol in a relocatable ELF object has st_value=0x10 and st_size=46; its .text section starts at file offset 0x40 with sh_addr=0. Which bytes should you extract?

options.A: 48 bytes from file offset 0x10, including the alignment padding.
options.B: 46 bytes from file offset 0x40, ignoring the symbol value.
options.C: 46 bytes from file offset 0x50, excluding the following padding.
options.D: 48 bytes from file offset 0x50, stopping at the next function.

questions.explanation: The start is sh_offset + st_value - sh_addr = 0x50. st_size supplies the 46-byte length; subsequent alignment padding is outside the symbol.

questions.text: The reader decodes r_info with symbol_index = r_info >> 32 and relocation_type = r_info & 0xffffffff. For r_info = (7 << 32) | 2, what pair does it produce?
questions.explanation: The shift extracts the high 32-bit symbol index, 7; the mask extracts the low 32-bit relocation type, 2.
